headline_verdict: The paper has a concrete NLP-agent contribution and reproducible headline aggregate arithmetic. The strongest remaining concern is heterogeneous initialization in the nominally common-initialization three-run component study. Main/appendix method and split differences, paired uncertainty and an unsupported backbone ceiling also need attention. A concurrent revision resolved the stale-PDF issue and improved baseline/evaluator/statistical documentation; those improvements are credited rather than reported as absent. This is an internal review, not an official ARR score or acceptance prediction.

review_form.summary: RouterBSI represents skill applicability as editable natural-language predicates, refines them from labeled routing failures, selects proposals by mean Boolean error on bounded per-skill replay and admits changes through held-out validation relative to the initial predicate. It evaluates routing, retention, downstream success and component/backbone variants across six SRA-Bench datasets.
strengths: Sections 3–4 provide a concrete language-agent routing problem and explicit natural-language predicates editable without changing model weights.
The average replay-loss equation and strict validation comparison against the INITIAL predicate are already correct; Figure 2 makes the update mechanism tangible.
Table 1 headline aggregate nDCG gains reproduce from saved data: 8.38% over SkillRouter, 29.25% over SkillDAG and 26.73% over Skill-Pro.
The 75.5% top-five recall and 90.5% relative retention headlines reproduce; the paper acknowledges TheoremQA/MedCalc-Bench exceptions and SkillDAG’s stronger downstream mean.
The appendix includes prompts, exact global split counts, gate/replay procedures, aggregate and per-dataset results, and a new matched-loss diagnostic. Limitations and ethics discussion are present.
weaknesses: ISSUE-002: The main replay definition omits the current failed task and does not distinguish bounded per-skill replay from the unbounded global history used by the implementation.
ISSUE-003: The main ranking rule describes arithmetic addition, while Appendix A.1 specifies selected-first lexicographic ordering.
ISSUE-004: The main per-dataset 70/15/15 statement contradicts the constrained global split in Appendix C.
ISSUE-005: The manifest-linked three-run ablation does not use common initial predicates across all configurations, contrary to the PDF and source claim.
ISSUE-007: The main superiority comparisons report point estimates without paired uncertainty; repeated-run dispersion is confined to a different ablation experiment.
ISSUE-009: Three backbone endpoints do not establish an irreducible predicate plateau or failure of more capable language models.
questions: Do the 12 manifest-linked initialization files represent the plotted historical runs? If not, supply immutable bindings; if yes, approve correction of the common-initialization claim.
Do the frozen retrieval and released SkillRouter descriptions in new Appendix D.4 apply to every reported run, and what are the two remaining main-listed model roles?
What roles did Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-5.4 serve in the reported experiments, and where are their bound configurations?
Are saved matched per-task predictions available for uncertainty analysis without new model calls?
What are the intended venue, cycle, submission stage, paper type, deadline and local-PDF/upload permissions?
Which proposed corrections/redesigns should be applied? Manuscript changes, builds and new experiments remain unapproved.

narrative_diagnostics.recoverable_thesis: Explicit, editable natural-language skill-applicability predicates can be improved from labeled routing failures using bounded per-skill replay selection and a cold-start held-out gate, while keeping model weights fixed.
narrative_diagnostics.front_page_assessment: Title and abstract identify feedback refinement, replay and gating; Figure 1 illustrates applicability versus topical similarity with single-day versus date-range coffee-price queries. It does not show optimization, but Figure 2 does. A mandatory Figure-1 redesign is not justified by narrative self-containment.
narrative_diagnostics.substantive_nlp_contribution: Selecting natural-language procedural context for LLM agents from task language is a concrete language-agent problem. The useful novelty is the specific editable routing state/update/validation combination, not generic recursion or a claimed theorem about Bayesian inference.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We propose RouterBSI, a non-parametric skill-routing framework that evaluates explicit applicability predicates over retrieved candidates, making routing criteria interpretable and directly editable without updating the underlying language model.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Explicit natural-language predicate interface and concrete examples.
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: Inspectability/editability is a representation property; no human-edit benefit was measured, and no such experiment is required for this modest claim.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We develop a recursive self-improvement procedure that refines predicates from routing failures, selects updates through minimum Bayes risk over a bounded replay of relevant and irrelevant tasks, and rejects updates with higher held-out validation error than the cold-start predicate.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Minimum-average-risk equation, initial-predicate gate and four component configurations.
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: The core equations are clear; operational main/appendix mismatches are NAR-001. Timing is iteration-end, not necessarily immediately after each local repair.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We evaluate RouterBSI on six SRA-Bench datasets with a shared 26K-skill corpus, achieving the highest aggregate nDCG@10 and Hit@1 among evaluated methods while ablations establish the contributions of replay and validation.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Table 1 aggregate nDCG@1/nDCG@10; Figures 3,5–7 and detailed tables.
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: Observed routing leadership is delivered and benchmark exceptions acknowledged. Hit@1 naming should align with nDCG@1. Downstream leadership is not claimed as this contribution and belongs to SkillDAG in the displayed means. Parent verification now establishes heterogeneous initialization in the three-run ablation; qualify establish the contributions rather than treating unmatched means as controlled evidence.

narrative_diagnostics.conclusion_assessment: All three contribution themes recur in §8. Strongest average routing and retention are claimed, while dependency-aware downstream improvement is future work; no missing conclusion revisit is found.
